summary: Peter Connolly is a scholar in religious studies and Indology who earned his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University. In 1980, he served as a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester.

Peter D. Hershock works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University and under traditional teachers Seungsahn and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim, later directing the Asian Studies Development Program at the East-West Center (attested 2007–2013).
Peter Ebbatson is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Oxford under the doctoral supervision of Walpola Rahula.

Peter Fenner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held a post at Deakin University. He studied under traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche as well as advisers Noble Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch.

Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He held an appointment at Utrecht University from around 1968 to 1975 and served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1975 to 1998.

Peter Gyallay-Pap works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the London School of Economics and Political Science in 1990 and was an adjunct at Adams State University as attested in 2007.

Peter Harvey works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, and founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996. Attested between 2002 and 2015, he was an Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland.
Peter Haskel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed graduate studies at Columbia University, where he studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter James Gilks works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and completed a PhD at Australian National University (attested 2010) under supervisor John Powers and several traditional and academic teachers.

Peter Koret is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who completed a doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London. He has held academic posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter M. Scharf (b. 1957) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona, also studying under Shree Narayan Mishra, Ludo Rocher, and Narendranath Pandey.
Peter Masefield specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under supervisors L. P. N. Perera and Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

Peter Moran is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Tufts University and completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Charles F. Keyes, alongside several traditional and academic teachers.

Peter N. Gregory (b. 1945) works in Buddhist studies and sinology, having earned his Ph.D. at Harvard in 1981 under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held posts at Illinois, Kuroda Institute, and Smith College as Jill Ker Conway Professor (attested 2005).
Peter Schwabland works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA at the University of Washington under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger (b. 1952) is a scholar of Tibetology who studied under Dieter Schuh from around 1974 to 1981. He succeeded Klaus Sagaster in 2001 and served as a professor at the University of Bonn from circa 2002 to 2018.

Peter Skilling, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2004). He founded the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and has held posts at EFEO, Chulalongkorn University, and several visiting professorships.

Peter Stewart (b. 1971) specializes in Indology and history and archaeology. In 2011, he was associated with the Classical Art Research Centre and served around that time as Associate Professor of Classical Art and Archaeology at the University of Oxford.

Peter Zieme (b. 1942) is a scholar of linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the German Academy of Sciences at Berlin (~1969–1991) and the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1992–2007).

Peter van der Veer (b. 1953) studied at Groningen and Utrecht. A scholar of religious studies, Indology, and sinology, he held posts at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, University of Amsterdam, Utrecht University, and directed the MPI-MMG (~2009–2021).
